q205.question: What does the saying "the Most Highs rule in the kingdoms of men" mean: who rules, what is ruled, and how?
q205.answer:
"Most Highs" is the name given to the Vorondadek Sons who rule the constellations. These Sons are called the Most Highs because, when commissioned as constellation rulers, they embody the highest administrative wisdom, coupled with the most farseeing loyalty, of all the orders of the Local Universe Sons of God [43:3.1]. Therefore the saying "⟦Q 3:5.2⟧«Los Altísimos gobiernan en los reinos de los hombres».⟦/Q⟧" is not poetic rhetoric; it points to a fact of universe administration, namely that the Constellation Fathers actually oversee the affairs of the races and nations of the inhabited worlds [3:5.2, 43:5.16].

This rule, however, is exercised not in the inner life of the individual but on the level of groups and nations. The Urantia Book says plainly that the Most Highs "⟦Q 43:9.4⟧rule in the kingdoms of men rather than in the hearts of individuals⟦/Q⟧" [43:9.4].

1. Who Are the Most Highs?

In each constellation of Nebadon, Gabriel commissions at least three Vorondadek Sons as Most Highs; the presiding one is called the Constellation Father, and his two associates are the senior Most High and the junior Most High [43:3.2]. A Constellation Father rules for ten thousand standard years, that is, about 50,000 years of Urantia time [43:3.2]. No disaffection of the Vorondadek Sons has ever occurred in Nebadon [43:3.1]. On Edentia there is a Faithful of Days, a representative of the Paradise Trinity, who stands at the right hand of the Constellation Fathers, but he never offers advice unless it is asked for [43:4.1, 43:4.2].

2. What Do They Rule? Legislation and the Bounds of the Nations

The Constellation Fathers are little concerned with the individuals of the inhabited planets, but they are closely connected with the legislative and law-making functions that greatly concern all the mortal races and national groups [43:3.5]. When the prophet of old sang that the Most High "⟦Q 43:5.16⟧set the bounds of the people⟦/Q⟧" [43:5.16], he was recognizing, it is explained, the controlling hand of the Constellation Fathers in the affairs of nations. In planetary justice, too, no arbitrary execution is carried out without the consent of the Constellation Father, and the reason lies in this very principle [50:2.6].

3. A Special Relationship with Urantia: The Most High Observer

At the time of the Lucifer rebellion the Most Highs of Edentia took over certain phases of planetary authority over the rebel worlds, and they will continue to exercise this jurisdiction as long as Lucifer lives [43:3.7]. Every quarantined world has a Vorondadek Son stationed as an observer, and he does not intervene in planetary administration except when ordered by the Constellation Father. The Urantia Book says that it is actually this Most High observer who "⟦Q 43:5.17⟧rules in the kingdoms of men⟦/Q⟧" [43:5.17]. Such an observer has been stationed on this planet ever since the Caligastia betrayal, and Machiventa Melchizedek too paid him respectful homage [43:5.17]. Moreover, all Urantia affairs connected with Michael's bestowal were directly supervised by the Most Highs of Norlatiadek [43:3.8].

4. By What Means Do They Rule?

The Most Highs rule in the kingdoms of men through many celestial forces and agencies, but chiefly through the ministry of seraphim [114:0.1]. This does not mean, however, that human history should be viewed as a series of miracles. The Urantia Book warns that it is a mistake to regard theologic doctrines and religious superstitions as supernatural deposits that have come down miraculously into history [97:8.5]. It also says that the spiritual sovereignty of God overrides all intermediate loyalties, and that someday civil rulers too will learn that the Most Highs rule in the kingdoms of men [134:5.3].

Summary

"⟦Q 114:0.1⟧The Most Highs rule in the kingdoms of men⟦/Q⟧" means that the Vorondadek Sons of the constellation of Norlatiadek watch over the great currents of races and nations through legislation and supervision [43:3.5, 43:9.4]. On isolated Urantia a Most High observer is stationed, and the seraphim carry out this rule [43:5.17, 114:0.1]. The meaning of the saying is that it is not the heart of the individual but the history of the nations that stands under the supervision of the unseen Most Highs.

q206.question: What do ascenders learn on the seventy training worlds of Edentia, and why is that period called the most settled period?
q206.answer:
Ascenders who have graduated from Jerusem, the system capital, go on to the seventy training worlds of transition morontia culture that surround Edentia, the constellation headquarters. The heart of what they learn there is "group ethics," the secret of pleasurable and profitable interassociation among the different orders of intelligent personalities [43:8.2, 43:8.3]. In a word, it is the true socialization of the morontia personality [43:8.4].

This period is the most settled period in an ascending mortal's career up to the status of a finaliter, and The Urantia Book says, "⟦Q 43:8.2⟧this is really the typical morontia life⟦/Q⟧" [43:8.2].

1. Edentia's Place among the Stages of Ascent

On the mansion worlds the ascender completed the unification of the evolving mortal personality, and at the system capital he gained Jerusem citizenship and achieved the willingness to subject the self to the discipline of group activities [43:8.4]. Now, on the constellation training worlds, he must build true socialization on top of these [43:8.4]. On the system worlds he was more material than spiritual, and on Salvington he will become more spiritual, but the ascender on Edentia stands at the midpoint of the journey from evolutionary animal to ascending spirit [43:9.2].

2. Learning to Live with the Univitatia

The hosts of the Edentia worlds are the univitatia, beings who intellectually resemble morontia beings but who are very different in every other respect [43:8.6]. The ascender learns at the same time to live and work happily with ten morontia fellows and to co-operate wholeheartedly with ten univitatia [43:8.5, 43:8.6, 43:8.7]. On the first seven major worlds one ascender lives with ten univitatia; as the stages advance the number increases, until at last ten morontians live with ten univitatia [43:8.12].

3. The Seven Tasks of Socialization

The aim of the learning is to achieve intellectual harmony and vocational adjustment with both groups of fellows [43:8.8], and to master the ability to live in intimate contact with other beings "⟦Q 43:8.9⟧with ever-lessening irritability and ever-diminishing resentment⟦/Q⟧" [43:8.9]. The reversion directors contribute much to this attainment through their group-play activities [43:8.9]. Further, the ascender co-ordinates these socializing techniques with the Paradise career and develops the cosmic insight that grasps the eternal goal hidden within seemingly trivial time-space activities [43:8.10]. Finally, he brings all these procedures to a climax through group spiritual association, and it is said that two moral creatures in partnership do not merely double their possibilities of attainment but more nearly quadruple them [43:8.11].

4. Edentia Citizenship and the Paradise Assembly

After graduating from the seventieth world, ascenders take up residence on Edentia, and for the first time they take part in a "Paradise assembly," where they hear from the Faithful of Days the story of the career that lies ahead [43:9.1]. This constellation sojourn is the prespirit socialization training of the ascenders, similar in character to the prefinaliter experience of Havona and the preabsonite training on Paradise [43:9.3]. During this time ascenders serve in varied capacities in the constellation program concerned with group, racial, national, and planetary welfare [43:9.4].

Summary

The seventy worlds of Edentia are a school of socialization where the ascender learns to live and work joyfully together with beings different from himself [43:8.3, 43:8.4]. Because he passes from world to world without changing his body and without any break in consciousness, it is the most uniform and stable period [43:8.2, 43:9.3], and when he leaves he will look back on it as one of the most beautiful and refreshing epochs this side of Paradise [43:9.5]. It reminds us that learning to live with our neighbors now is practice for the eternal career.

q207.question: Who are the celestial artisans, and what becomes of the talents and longings that went unfulfilled on earth in the morontia career?
q207.answer:
The celestial artisans are the master artists and artisans of the morontia and lower spirit realms, spirits and semispirits who are engaged in morontia embellishment and in spiritual beautification [44:0.1]. They are not created as such; they are a selected corps made up of teacher personalities from Havona and of volunteer pupils from various celestial groups, ascending mortals among them [44:0.3]. And their story leads to a promise that our talents and longings which never came to flower on earth are by no means in vain [44:8.3, 44:8.4].

The Urantia Book emphasizes that "⟦Q 44:0.2⟧the morontia and spirit worlds are not without their high arts and supernal cultures⟦/Q⟧" [44:0.2].

1. Origin and Organization

The original teaching corps consisted of seven thousand Havona instructors assigned by the Infinite Spirit in co-operation with the Seven Master Spirits, one thousand for each of the seven artisan divisions [44:0.3]. Any morontia personality or spirit entity below the rank of inherent divine sonship may enter this corps, but no one may enlist for less than one thousand years [44:0.4]. Their chief realm of activity is in the constellations, especially on the seven hundred seventy worlds surrounding each headquarters [44:0.1].

2. The Seven Divisions

The celestial artisans work in seven divisions: the celestial musicians, the heavenly reproducers, the divine builders, the thought recorders, the energy manipulators, the designers and embellishers, and the harmony workers [44:0.5-12]. Their original teachers all came from Havona, where the patterns of spirit art are found [44:0.13]. Spirit melody is not material sound waves but spiritual pulsations received by the spirits of celestial personalities [44:1.1], and the harmony workers deal not with music or painting but with specialized forces and energies that are real in the spiritual world [44:7.1]. The revealer confesses that it is almost hopeless to convey this work in mortal language, yet he stresses the fact that it is real [44:0.20, 44:0.21].

3. Three Sources of Mortal Talent

Underneath every special human ability there is always an inherent aptitude, and special abilities are never arbitrary gifts of the Gods [44:8.2]. To this may be added the guidance of the indwelling Adjuster drawing on actual experience gained on other worlds, and where both are outstanding, spirit artisans are commissioned to help harmonize these gifts [44:8.2]. The celestial artisans do not work directly on worlds such as Urantia, but they sometimes come from the system headquarters to assist gifted individuals [44:8.1].

4. What Becomes of Unfulfilled Longings?

There is no caste in the ranks of the spirit artisans, and however lowly one's origin, ability receives due recognition [44:8.3]. The Urantia Book says, "⟦Q 44:8.3⟧No puede haber obstáculos de herencia humana ni privación de medio ambiente mortal que la carrera morontial no compense plenamente y elimine enteramente.⟦/Q⟧" [44:8.3]. Of course, many ambitions of the flesh are selfish and are socialized and fade away; but if, after acquiring true mota insight, you still desire to do something, you will most certainly be granted every opportunity fully to satisfy that longing [44:8.4]. Before leaving the local universe, ascenders will be satiated respecting every true intellectual, artistic, and social longing [44:8.5].

Summary

The celestial artisans are a volunteer corps who bring the beauty of Havona to the worlds of space [44:0.3, 44:0.13], and their existence shows that beauty is part of eternal reality. The Gods do not arbitrarily distribute talents, but they do provide for the satisfaction of every noble longing [44:8.3]. To anyone who has had to fold away a dream because of circumstances, this offers great comfort: if it is a true longing, the opportunity will surely come in the eternal career [44:8.4].

q208.question: What is the training ascenders receive on Jerusem in the homes of the Material Sons and Daughters, and what is the education in the Melchizedek schools?
q208.answer:
Jerusem, the system capital, is where ascending mortals make up for experience they failed to gain in the life in the flesh and prepare to assume responsibilities as citizens of the universe. The two pillars of this training are the "Adamic training of the ascenders" in the homes of the Material Sons and Daughters, and the schools conducted by the Melchizedeks [45:6.2, 45:7.3].

The Material Sons and Daughters are the immediate sponsors and teachers of ascenders from the time they gain citizenship on the headquarters world until they depart for Edentia [45:6.2]. The Melchizedeks are the leaders of the great teaching corps that functions on Jerusem and its associated worlds, including the mansion worlds [45:7.1].

1. What Is Gained in the Homes of the Material Sons and Daughters

The Material Sons and Daughters are very much like our material sex races, and ascenders find many interests in common with them [45:6.1]. On the mansion worlds nearly every deficiency due to heredity, environment, or a prematurely terminated life is made up, with the exception of experience related to the sex life [45:6.3]. Mortals deficient in sex experience can make up the social, intellectual, emotional, and spiritual aspects of that deficiency by living as members of the families of the Material Sons and Daughters [45:6.3].

2. Why Parental Experience Is Indispensable

The Urantia Book says that no surviving mortal, midwayer, or seraphim may ascend to Paradise and be mustered into the Corps of the Finality without having passed through the experience of parental relationship to an evolving child, or some equivalent experience [45:6.4]. The reason is that "⟦Q 45:6.4⟧La relación entre el hijo y el padre es fundamental en el concepto esencial del Padre Universal y de sus hijos del universo.⟦/Q⟧" [45:6.4]. Mortals who have not experienced parenthood must therefore complete this training in the homes of the Material Sons on Jerusem [45:6.6], and even the nonreproducing midwayers and seraphim gain this experience by helping to rear the offspring of the Adams and Eves [45:6.5]. Those who have children in the probationary nursery on the finaliters' world may also serve there as associate parents and so fulfill one half of this training [45:6.8].

3. The Melchizedek Schools and Training for Representative Government

The mansion worlds are where those who did not fuse with their Adjusters in the life in the flesh are given the opportunity to continue their interrupted spiritual attainment, and they must learn to make their own the traits they failed to acquire during the life in the flesh [45:7.1]. The Melchizedeks conduct upward of thirty educational centers on Jerusem, beginning with the college of self-evaluation and ending with the schools of Jerusem citizenship [45:7.3]. Here ascenders qualify to assume the responsibilities of representative government, and The Urantia Book says, "⟦Q 45:7.3⟧El gobierno representativo es el ideal divino del autogobierno entre los seres no perfectos.⟦/Q⟧" [45:7.3].

4. Suffrage According to Mota

On Jerusem suffrage is universal, but votes are cast in a graded manner, from one to a thousand votes, according to the recognized and recorded mota, that is, the degree of possession of morontia wisdom [45:7.6]. Citizens are judged as to morontia wisdom, spirit insight, and socialization experience before the Melchizedek examiners, the testing corps of the Brilliant Evening Stars, and the Twenty-four Counselors respectively [45:7.7]. Those slow in personality unification receive intensive training from the Material Sons, and no one leaves for the constellation until the attainment of mota personality has been demonstrated [45:7.8].

Summary

The training on Jerusem is a process in which the home and parental experience missed on earth is made up in the homes of the Material Sons and Daughters [45:6.3, 45:6.6], and wisdom and the capacity for self-government are developed in the Melchizedek schools so that ascenders become citizens of representative government [45:7.3, 45:7.6]. The teaching that parenthood is the foundation for understanding the Universal Father reminds us that the experiences we go through in our homes now have eternal meaning [45:6.4].

q209.question: What kind of world is Jerusem, the system capital, and what do ascenders see there?
q209.answer:
Jerusem is the headquarters world of the system of Satania; it is not an evolutionary planet but an architectural sphere designed and built from the beginning. The Urantia Book says that Jerusem gives a foretaste of the glory and grandeur of Paradise, while also stressing that this first stopping world of the Paradise journey is far more material than spiritual [46:2.6, 46:2.7].

1. Sky, Light, and Climate

On Jerusem there is neither day nor night, and no seasons of heat and cold [46:1.4]. Energy projected upward by the power transformers is reflected from the ceiling of the electric atmosphere, becoming a soft, even light similar to Urantia sunlight at about ten o'clock in the morning [46:1.4]. The light does not come from one place but is sifted down from the whole sky; for this reason such headquarters worlds do not shine in space and cannot be seen even from close by [46:1.5]. The illumination is maintained for seventy-five per cent of the day, after which it dims to about the brightness of a full moon, and this is the quiet hour of rest for all Jerusem [46:1.7]. Worlds such as Jerusem also do not suffer from solar disturbances or the problems of a cooling sun [46:1.8].

2. Land, Water, and Life

Because there are no earthquakes and no rain on Jerusem, there are no rugged mountain ranges, but there are beautiful highlands, and vast areas are preserved in the "natural state" [46:2.1]. There are tens of thousands of little lakes but no rushing rivers or wide oceans, and moisture condenses and falls each day as the light recedes [46:2.2]. The atmosphere is a mixture of three gases, with a gas added that is suited to the respiration of morontia life [46:2.3]. Above all, since there is no organic evolution on Jerusem, there are no warring forms of life, no struggle for existence, and no survival of the fittest; instead there is a creative adaptation that foreshadows the harmony of the central universe [46:2.5].

3. Arrival and the Circles

Ascenders arrive by transport seraphim on the crystal field called the "sea of glass" [46:2.9]. The major groups of universe life are domiciled in residential reservations in the form of concentric circles called the Jerusem circles; there are seven such circles: those of the Sons of God, the angels, the universe aids, the Master Physical Controllers, the ascending mortals, the courtesy colonies, and the finaliter corps [46:5.1-8]. At the center of the circles of the Sons stands the Michael memorial, commemorating Michael's bestowal on Urantia, and at its dedication all Jerusem heard this moving story [46:5.19].

4. What Will Claim the Ascender's Attention

The promenade surrounding the circles of the angels holds a vast exhibit showing the advancing status of the peopled worlds of Satania, and the revealer says that this will be the first sight to claim the ascender's attention [46:5.23]. At the center of the circles of the ascending mortals are 619 planetary memorials, and in their midst is a working model of Edentia [46:5.27]. In the circles of the finaliters stands a vacant temple bearing the inscription "⟦Q 46:5.32⟧«Aún no dedicado, reservado para la séptima etapa del espíritu — para una asignación eterna».⟦/Q⟧" [46:5.32], which shows that at the end of the ascent there lies a destiny not yet revealed. The activities of Jerusem consist of work, progress, and play, that is, service, study, and relaxation [46:5.29].

Summary

Jerusem is an architectural world with an even, soft light, a climate without rain or storms, and a creative life free of the struggle for existence [46:1.4, 46:2.1, 46:2.5]. There ascenders see many orders of beings at work, meet the Michael memorial that commemorates Urantia and the exhibits of their home worlds, and begin a balanced life of service, study, and relaxation [46:5.19, 46:5.23, 46:5.29].

q210.question: What happens to children who die young? Please tell me about the probationary nursery on the finaliters' world.
q210.answer:
The Urantia Book teaches that children who die at an early age do not simply vanish; under certain conditions they are repersonalized, grow up, and are given the opportunity to choose the eternal path for themselves. The place where this happens is the probationary nursery on the finaliter world, the first of the Jerusem transition-culture spheres, that is, the infant-receiving schools of Satania [47:2.1].

These schools are institutions devoted to the nurture and training of children who died on the evolutionary worlds before acquiring individual status on the universe records [47:2.1].

1. The Survival of the Parents Is the Key

If either or both of such a child's parents survive, the guardian of destiny deputizes her associated cherubim as the custodian of the child's potential identity [47:2.1]. In other words, if even one of the natural parents ascends, the child is accorded repersonalization on the system finaliter planet [45:6.7]. The child's awakening occurs at the exact time of the parent's arrival on the first mansion world, and children are personalized exactly as of their physical status at the time of death, except for reproductive potential [47:2.2].

2. Life in the Nursery

The children are grouped according to whether or not they have Adjusters [47:2.3]. Children of pre-Adjuster age, from under one year to about five years, are cared for in families of five [47:2.3], and Adjuster-indwelt children also grow up in families of five, ranging in age from six to fourteen [47:2.5]. The children are reared in the families of the Material Sons and their associates [47:2.4], and the nursery is supervised by one thousand couples of volunteer Material Sons and Daughters, assisted by midsonite parental groups [45:6.9]. Guardian seraphim minister to them spiritually, and spornagia to their physical needs [47:2.6]. Ascenders deficient in parental experience may, by permit, serve here as associate parents to their own and other children [45:6.8].

3. A Choice of Their Own

These children are given every opportunity to choose the heavenly way just as they would have made such a choice on the worlds where death so untimely terminated their careers [47:2.2]. If they make the final choice at any time after sixteen, they translate to the first mansion world and begin the Paradise ascent; some choose earlier, but very few children under sixteen years of age by Urantia reckoning are found on the mansion worlds [47:2.5]. The children appear as they did on their native world except for the absence of sex differentiation, and there is no reproduction of mortal kind after the life on the inhabited worlds [45:6.7]. The children grow up on this transition world until they make their final choice [47:2.6]. But if they do not choose the ascendant life, or if they definitely decide against the Havona adventure, their probationary careers end, and The Urantia Book says, "⟦Q 47:2.7⟧Simplemente llegan a ser como si no hubiesen sido.⟦/Q⟧" [47:2.7]. The choice remains to the end a matter of free will.

4. Their Destiny

Children who choose the Paradise path go on to the first mansion world, and many of them arrive in time to join their parents in the Havona ascent [47:2.8]. After passing through Havona and attaining the Deities, they become the permanent ascendant citizenship of Paradise [47:2.8]. Because they were deprived of the valuable evolutionary experience on the mortal worlds, however, they are not mustered into the Corps of the Finality [47:2.8].

Summary

A child who dies young, if even one parent survives, is repersonalized in the probationary nursery on the finaliters' world, grows up under the care of the Material Sons and Daughters and the seraphim, and is given the opportunity to choose the heavenly way for himself [47:2.1, 47:2.2, 45:6.7]. This teaching is a deep comfort to parents who have lost children, and at the same time it reminds them of the solemn fact that this comfort is bound up with the parents' own survival [47:2.2, 47:2.8].

q211.question: Who governs the system of Satania now after the Lucifer rebellion, and how? And what are the seven transitional culture worlds that circle Jerusem?
q211.answer:
Our local system, Satania, has been governed since Lucifer's rebellion by his successor, the System Sovereign Lanaforge [45:3.2]. A System Sovereign is a primary Lanonandek Son, the chief executive of a local system made up of inhabited worlds [45:2.1]. Since the rebellion Satania has been run by an expanded emergency administration of seven Lanonandeks and by an executive council of twelve members [45:3.9], and around Jerusem circle the seven transitional culture worlds that ascenders visit from their mansion world days onward [45:1.1].

1. The Wide Discretion of System Sovereigns, and Rebellion

The System Sovereigns of Nebadon are entrusted with great executive responsibility and unusual personal discretion; not all universes, even within Orvonton, are organized in this way [45:2.1]. Yet in the history of Nebadon these executives have shown disloyalty only three times, and the Lucifer rebellion in Satania was the last and the most extensive [45:2.1]. Even so, no change was made in the technique of system administration after the rebellion, and the present Sovereign exercises all the powers held by his predecessor, except for certain matters which the Ancients of Days have not yet fully restored, and which remain under the supervision of the Constellation Fathers [45:2.2, 43:3.7].

2. What Kind of Ruler Is Lanaforge?

The Urantia Book introduces Lanaforge thus: "⟦Q 45:2.3⟧El jefe actual de Satania es un gobernante brillante y compasivo, y es un soberano que ha sido probado por la rebelión.⟦/Q⟧" [45:2.3]. At the time of the second system rebellion in Nebadon, when his superior fell into darkness, he, as first assistant, seized the reins of government, so that comparatively few personalities were lost [45:2.3]. He is the only primary Lanonandek Son in all Nebadon who served Michael loyally in the very presence of the default of his brother of superior rank [45:2.3]. Although the affairs of the isolated worlds have not yet been returned to his jurisdiction, he shows great interest in the welfare of these worlds and frequently visits Urantia [45:2.4].

3. The Emergency Administration and the Executive Council

Ordinarily a System Sovereign is supported by two or three Lanonandek assistants, but Satania is at present administered by a staff of seven Lanonandeks [45:3.1]. Among them are the custodian of the system, the holder of interned spirits, and the bestowal director, who supervises the activities transplanted to Jerusem since Michael's bestowal on Urantia [45:3.5, 45:3.7]. Since the system is a unit of administration, not adjudication, there are only minor courts on Jerusem, and the executive council of twelve members serves as the supreme advisory body [45:3.9]. Representation on the supreme council of the universe is suspended because of rebellion, but since Michael's bestowal the election of members to the Edentia legislature has been resumed [45:3.22]. Every ten days the Sovereign holds purely social and spiritual gatherings with many orders of beings on the sea of glass [45:2.5, 45:2.6].

4. The Seven Transitional Culture Worlds

The seven worlds circling Jerusem are the finaliter world, the morontia world, the angelic world, the superangel world, the world of the Sons, the world of the Spirit, and the world of the Father [45:1.2-9]. Mansion world sojourners visit the finaliter world at least once a year, where they catch a fleeting glimpse of the finaliters who have completed the Paradise ascent and returned, and they gain the assurance that they too can finish that course [45:1.2]. With each mansion world attained, one becomes qualified to visit the next transition world [45:1.4]. The seventh, the world of the Father, is a silent sphere where no one dwells, and in the central temple of light all beings are welcome as worshipers [45:1.9]. Its satellites are now used as detention spheres confining the interned groups of the Lucifer rebellion [45:1.10], and ascenders from the seventh mansion world visit there to view, as a solemn warning, those who rejected Michael's salvation [45:1.11].

Summary

Satania is governed by Lanaforge, tested by rebellion and proved loyal, together with an emergency administration of seven Lanonandeks and a council of twelve members [45:2.3, 45:3.1, 45:3.9]. The seven transitional culture worlds circling Jerusem are places of assurance, fellowship, and worship for ascenders, and at the same time places of warning that show the outcome of rebellion [45:1.2, 45:1.9, 45:1.11].

q212.question: Is there humor and play in the morontia life as well? Please tell me what the reversion directors do.
q212.answer:
Yes. The Urantia Book says that there are morontia and spiritual equivalents of mirth and laughter, and that the ascending career is divided almost equally between work and play [48:4.1]. Celestial rest and humor differ from the human kind but are truly enjoyed, and there ideal humor accomplishes the very thing it does on earth [48:4.2]. Those in charge of this rest and humor are the reversion directors.

1. Who Are the Reversion Directors?

The reversion directors are not a created group; they are a recruited volunteer corps embracing many beings, from Havona natives down through the ministering spirits of time to the morontia progressors from the evolutionary worlds [48:4.9]. They help their fellows achieve thought change and mind rest, because such attitudes are most helpful in recuperating depleted energies [48:4.9]. They are called "reversion" directors because they help revert the memory to a former state of development, so that past events may be lived over again [48:4.10]. On Edentia, too, they contribute much to the socialization of ascenders through group play [43:8.9].

2. What Spirit Humor Is Not

Spirit jesting is never tinged with the coloring of highlighting the misfortunes of the weak and erring, nor does it blaspheme the righteousness and glory of divinity [48:4.4]. The Urantia Book points out that we have mixed the vulgar and the unkind with our humor, yet it says that we are to be congratulated on having a relatively keen sense of humor [48:4.13].

3. Three Levels of Humor

The first is reminiscent jesting, the drollery that lightens present burdens by recalling past struggles and foolish anxieties [48:4.5]. The second is present humor, the joy of discovering that many things which caused us grave concern are unimportant [48:4.6]. The third is prophetic joy, the satisfaction that grows out of the assurance "⟦Q 48:4.7⟧that all things work together for good⟦/Q⟧" [48:4.7] and out of faith in the loving overcare of our superiors.

4. Why Humor Is Needed

One of the functions of humor is to help us take ourselves less seriously, and The Urantia Book says, "⟦Q 48:4.15⟧El humorismo es el antídoto divino contra la exaltación del ego.⟦/Q⟧" [48:4.15]. Humor is an automatic safety valve against the pressure of unremitting self-contemplation and the struggle for achievement, and it cushions the shock of unexpected facts and truths [48:4.18]. Primitive man has no capacity for humor, and Paradise beings have no need of it, but ascending beings struggling upward have the greatest need of it [48:4.16, 48:4.17]. Earthly humor, though crude, is valuable as insurance of health and as release of emotional pressure [48:4.19]. On the other hand, beings such as the inherent creators or the strictly businesslike power centers have no need of such reversion, and on Paradise the nature of worship does away with the need for reversion activities [48:4.11, 48:4.16]. Interestingly, all Satania is said to benefit in its play times from the cheerful humor of the corps of reversion directors who hail from Urantia, and the celestial sense of humor guards against the overgrowth of the idea of self-importance [48:4.14].

5. Memory Is the Basis of Laughter

Humor and play are always an echo of a look backward, a reminiscence of the past [48:4.19]. Because ascenders retain the memory of their former existence, they continue to enjoy the celestial equivalent of earthly humor, and the Adjuster adds the overtones of divinity to its joyful expression [48:4.20].

Summary

In the morontia career work and play are in balance, and the reversion directors refresh ascenders with rest that revives memory and with noble humor [48:4.1, 48:4.10]. Humor that does not belittle others, and laughter that lets us lay down self-importance, give a healthy balance to our life of faith even now [48:4.4, 48:4.15].

q213.question: In keeping with the saying "the work is important, but the self is not," what do the transition seraphim of the mansion worlds teach ascenders?
q213.answer:
On the mansion worlds angels of all orders serve, but those more fully assigned to this work are the transition ministers, the sixth order of seraphim. They help material mortal creatures pass over from the life in the flesh to the morontia existence of the seven mansion worlds [48:6.1]. Their teachings contain not only the techniques of ascension but also deep wisdom about one's inner attitude, and the lesson "the work is important, but the self is not" is one of its core teachings [48:6.37].

The morontia life actually begins on earth, at the moment the soul is conceived as the Adjuster indwells the moral mind, but we do not become conscious of the ministry of these seraphim until we reach the mansion worlds [48:6.2, 48:6.3].

1. Seven Divisions of Ministry

The transition ministers serve in seven divisions: seraphic evangels, racial interpreters, mind planners, morontia counselors, technicians, recorder-teachers, and ministering reserves [48:6.3, 48:6.4, 48:6.22, 48:6.24, 48:6.27, 48:6.29, 48:6.30, 48:6.34]. The seraphic evangels help ascenders choose wisely among many routes, while respecting freewill choice as long as it is not harmful [48:6.5, 48:6.6]. The mind planners do not take advantage of their pupils' ignorance to manipulate them; they respect the newborn morontia will [48:6.25].

2. Good Is Never Lost

The seraphic evangels proclaim the law of the conservation and dominance of goodness. Its content is that "⟦Q 48:6.7⟧No act of good is ever wholly lost⟦/Q⟧" [48:6.7]; a good act may be long thwarted, but it is eternally potent in proportion to the divinity of its motivation [48:6.7]. The mind planners also teach the eternal truth that even on earth, when our minds do not serve us well, we may exchange them for the mind of Jesus of Nazareth, who always serves us well [48:6.26].

3. Fact and Truth, Knowledge and Heart

The morontia counselors teach how to integrate meanings and unify values, and mota is to philosophy as two eyes are to one [48:6.27, 48:6.28]. The recorder-teachers teach us to seek truth as well as fact, and to learn to water the gardens of the heart and not only the dry sands of knowledge [48:6.32]. They also warn that one may be technically right as to fact and everlastingly wrong in truth [48:6.33].

4. On Disappointment and Self-Importance

The angels of the ministering reserves teach how pressure may produce stability and how to accept challenges without complaint, and they point out that the most disappointing disappointments sometimes become the greatest blessings [48:6.35, 48:6.36]. The way to suffer less through sorrow is to make fewer personal plans concerning other personalities and to accept one's lot after faithfully performing one's duty [48:6.36]. And they say, "⟦Q 48:6.37⟧Self-importance, not work-importance, exhausts immature creatures⟦/Q⟧" [48:6.37]. If we spend our energy on keeping up the dignity of the ego, little strength is left for the work, but if we leave ourselves out, we can do several things as easily as one [48:6.37].

Summary

The transition seraphim are the angels who help ascenders on the mansion worlds in choosing their path, organizing their minds, gaining the insight of mota, adjusting to a new environment, and pursuing records and truth [48:6.3, 48:6.27, 48:6.29]. Their teachings converge on the assurance that no good act is ever lost, and on the wisdom of setting the self aside and being faithful to the work of the world in which we now live [48:6.7, 48:6.37]. These lessons can already be practiced here on earth.

q214.question: How do mortals on other inhabited worlds differ from us, and how are they alike? Please also tell me what it means that man is not an evolutionary accident.
q214.answer:
The Urantia Book says that there are countless inhabited worlds in the universe, and that all of them are "evolutionary cradles" of the mortal races [49:0.1]. The forms of life differ greatly from world to world, but the minds and spiritual destinies of will-endowed mortals are remarkably alike [49:4.8]. And because all this diversity stands under law and order, man is not a product of chance [49:1.6].

1. Not Chance but Law and Order

The Urantia Book says plainly, "⟦Q 49:1.6⟧El hombre mortal no es un accidente evolucionario.⟦/Q⟧" [49:1.6]. Cosmic evolution is not always predictable, but it is strictly nonaccidental [49:1.1], and there is a precise system, a universal law, that determines the unfolding of the planetary life plan [49:1.6]. Time and the mass production of a species are not the controlling factors, and the example is given that mice reproduce faster than elephants, yet elephants evolve faster [49:1.6]. Planetary evolution is orderly and controlled, and the superior strains of life must be carefully protected [49:1.7].

2. Life Differs from World to World

Each planet has its own scale of life, and no two worlds have exactly the same plants and animals; this is not caprice but follows the decisions of the Life Carriers [49:1.3]. Life may begin from one center or from three, and it usually originates in the seas, though not always [49:1.4]. There are seven physical types and thousands upon thousands of varieties [49:2.1], and there are even nonbreathers who live on worlds with little or no atmosphere [49:3.1]. Because Urantia is an experimental planet, forms of life appeared here that are found nowhere else, and some common species are missing [49:5.11]. Life spans also vary, from twenty-five years on primitive worlds to nearly five hundred years on older spheres [49:4.6].

3. What All Mortals Have in Common

All mortals of will dignity are erect bipeds, animals that stand on two feet [49:4.1], and there are six basic evolutionary races [49:4.2]. All animal types develop from the patterns of preceding plant life [49:1.5]. On advanced worlds man and woman are equal in mind and spiritual status, and The Urantia Book says that a planet is not regarded as having emerged from barbarism as long as one sex seeks to tyrannize over the other [49:4.4]. Above all, mind is the bestowal of the Infinite Spirit and functions identically in every environment, so the mental life of all mortals, and their immediate career after death, are very similar [49:4.8].

4. The Single Condition of Survival

The Urantia Book, however, says, "⟦Q 49:4.9⟧Pero la mente mortal sin el espíritu inmortal no puede sobrevivir.⟦/Q⟧" [49:4.9]. Survival depends on spiritualization through the ministry of the Adjuster, on the birth and evolution of the immortal soul; at the least, there must be no antagonism toward the Adjuster's mission [49:4.9]. Mortals of the one-brained, two-brained, and three-brained types stand on an equal footing in the ascension career and must pass the same spiritual tests [49:5.18]. The differences in spirit receptivity associated with the pituitary body likewise do not survive natural death [49:5.20].

Summary

Life on the inhabited worlds differs greatly in atmosphere, physical type, life span, and racial makeup [49:1.3, 49:2.1, 49:4.6], but all this diversity stands under the wise plans of the Life Carriers and the laws of the universe [49:1.3, 49:1.6]. All mortals receive the same bestowal of mind and survive under the same spiritual conditions [49:4.8, 49:4.9], and so we are members of a universe family walking the same path as countless brother worlds.

q215.question: On a normal world, how are the schools of the Planetary Prince run, and through what seven epochs does civilization develop?
q215.answer:
The Planetary Prince is installed as ruler of the planet before the Life Carriers depart, and when human groups appear he is charged with inaugurating human civilization and drawing human society together [49:5.22, 49:5.23]. His work is designed to foster the development of planetary civilization independently of the missions of the Paradise Sons, and a loyal Prince remains permanently attached to the planet of his original assignment [50:5.1]. The center of this undertaking is the schools at the planetary headquarters, and its fruit is the progress of civilization through seven epochs.

1. Life in the Prince's Schools

The corporeal staff of the Prince organize the planetary schools of training and culture, where the best of the evolving races are educated and then sent back to teach improved methods to their own peoples [50:4.1]. Students and teachers alike were farmers and horticulturists [50:4.3], and their time was divided roughly equally among physical labor, social activities, educational application, vocational training, and spiritual culture [50:4.4-8]. Vocational training included schools of marriage and the home, training in arts and crafts, and courses for the training of teachers [50:4.7].

2. The Invisible Prince and the Test of Faith

The Planetary Prince is not visible to mortals, and believing the representations of his staff is a test of faith [50:4.9]. Nevertheless, the schools are so well adapted to the needs of each planet that a laudable rivalry for admission soon develops among the races [50:4.9]. As the trained children return to their own groups and establish new centers of learning, the civilizing influence spreads slowly but surely [50:4.10].

3. The Seven Epochs of Civilization

The races of an average world pass through the following epochs in succession [50:5.3].

The nutrition epoch: Primitive man is chiefly occupied with the problem of food [50:5.4].

The security age: When there is some leisure, men devote themselves to increasing security, and the clan is consolidated by mutual fear and hatred of outside groups [50:5.5].

The material-comfort era: Luxuries compete with necessities; this era is often marked by tyranny and dissipation, but the weak pleasure seekers are conquered by the truth-loving elements [50:5.6].

The quest for knowledge and wisdom: The effort to put knowledge into practice produces wisdom, and education is the watchword of this age [50:5.7].

The epoch of philosophy and brotherhood: Men become truly moral beings, establish the brotherhood of man, and learn to live by the golden rule [50:5.8].

The age of spiritual striving: Religion ascends from fear and superstition to cosmic wisdom and personal spiritual experience, and men become "exquisitely God-knowing" [50:5.9].

The era of light and life: Physical security, intellectual expansion, social culture, and spiritual achievement are co-ordinated in cosmic unity and unselfish service [50:5.10].

4. Culture and the Situation on Urantia

The Urantia Book says, "⟦Q 50:6.4⟧Culture presupposes quality of mind⟦/Q⟧" [50:6.4], and that inferior minds will spurn the highest culture even when it is handed to them ready-made. Even an ideal world is no life of comfort in a flower garden; there is always struggle in the early stages [50:6.3]. On Urantia the plan was proceeding smoothly until Caligastia joined the rebellion and perverted the teachings of the schools, bringing it to an end [50:4.11, 50:4.12], but the descendants of the loyal ones prevented the complete extinction of spiritual truth [50:4.13].

Summary

The Planetary Prince of a normal world spreads civilization by training the best of the races through labor, education, and spiritual culture in the headquarters schools [50:4.1, 50:4.10]. Civilization passes through nutrition, security, comfort, knowledge, brotherhood, and spiritual striving, and arrives at light and life [50:5.3-10]. This pattern sheds light on where our own society stands today and on what it should be moving toward.

q216.question: Are there any compensations or advantages in being born on a world isolated by rebellion, like Urantia? Please tell me what an "agondonter" is.
q216.answer:
There are. At first glance an isolated world such as Urantia seems most unfortunate, since it is deprived of the beneficent presence of superhuman personalities such as a Planetary Prince and a Material Son and Daughter [50:7.1]. But The Urantia Book teaches that this very isolation provides a special opportunity for the exercise of faith and for the development of a unique confidence in cosmic reliability that does not depend on sight [50:7.1]. Ascenders who have grown in this way are called "agondonters" [50:7.2].

1. The Reality of Isolation

As a result of the Lucifer rebellion, all the worlds of Satania were under the spiritual ban of Norlatiadek for two hundred thousand years, and it will take age upon age to retrieve these handicaps [50:6.5]. Because of the double tragedy of a rebellious Planetary Prince and a defaulting Material Son, Urantia still pursues a checkered course, and even Michael's bestowal did not immediately remove the temporal consequences of these blunders [50:6.5]. Compared with the loyal worlds, this planet seems far behind in intellectual progress and spiritual attainment [50:6.2].

2. The Opportunity for Faith That Believes without Seeing

Even on a normal world, believing in the invisible staff of the Prince is a test of faith [50:4.9], but on an isolated world even such visible help is lacking. In this very lack people can develop a faith that does not depend on material considerations [50:7.1]. The Urantia Book says that mortals from the quarantined worlds may eventually turn out to be "extremely fortunate" [50:7.1].

3. Who Are the Agondonters?

On Jerusem the ascenders from the isolated worlds occupy a residential sector by themselves, and they are called agondonters, meaning evolutionary will creatures "⟦Q 50:7.2⟧who can believe without seeing, persevere when isolated, and triumph over insuperable difficulties even when alone⟦/Q⟧" [50:7.2]. Their functional grouping persists throughout the local universe and the superuniverse; it disappears for a time in Havona but reappears upon the attainment of Paradise and persists even in the Corps of the Finality [50:7.2]. Tabamantia, the finaliter of Satania who inspects the experimental worlds, is likewise an agondonter from a quarantined sphere involved in the first rebellion [50:7.2, 49:5.12].

4. Special Assignments and Just Rewards

Such ascenders are very early intrusted with numerous special assignments where unquestioned faith and sublime confidence are essential [50:7.1]. Throughout the Paradise career, rewards follow effort as effect follows cause; these rewards distinguish the individual and contribute to the versatility of the ultimate activities of the finaliters [50:7.3]. Moreover, even amid the confusion left by the rebellion, the supervision of the Most Highs [43:5.16, 43:5.17] and the labors of the loyal have preserved the truth [50:4.13]. It is said that all beings who withstood the test of the Lucifer rebellion were immediately advanced in administrative status and enhanced in spiritual value [54:6.5]. And whatever hardship we may suffer through the wrongdoing of another or through the rebellion of the system, it is only temporary suffering and cannot in the least deprive us of our divine right to the Paradise ascent and the attainment of God [54:6.4].

Summary

Urantia's isolation is certainly a misfortune, but because of it we have gained a unique opportunity to develop a faith that believes without seeing and perseveres alone [50:7.1]. Those who triumph through such faith are the agondonters; they take on special universe assignments that require confidence, and they retain that identity even on Paradise [50:7.1, 50:7.2]. This is an encouragement that trusting God now, without visible evidence, itself has eternal value.

q217.question: On a normal world, how does the biologic uplift mission of the Planetary Adam and Eve proceed, and what are the "seven fathers"?
q217.answer:
The Planetary Adam and Eve are a Material Son and Daughter sent by the System Sovereign, and they always appear on a planet when primitive man has developed as high as possible on the biologic scale [52:3.1]. They are potentially the full gift of physical grace to the mortal races, and their chief duty is to multiply and uplift the children of time [51:3.3]. On Urantia this plan miscarried early [51:5.4], but by looking at how the mission proceeds on a normal world we can learn the original design God has prepared for mankind.

1. Building the Garden and the Violet Race

The Material Son and Daughter build a garden home on a site selected by the Planetary Prince, and these gardens are called Gardens of Eden in honor of Edentia, the constellation capital [51:3.1, 51:3.2]. Adam and Eve do not mingle at once with the native peoples; for many generations they remain biologically segregated and build up a strong race of their own order, and this is the origin of the violet race [51:3.3]. The plans for racial improvement are prepared by the Planetary Prince and his staff and executed by Adam and Eve [51:3.4]. The secondary midway creatures, too, are peculiar to the Adamic mission and contribute greatly to the development of civilization [51:3.6].

2. The Manner of Racial Blending

The violet race usually does not blend with the native races until its numbers exceed one million [51:5.2]. On a normal world the Planetary Adam and Eve themselves never mate with the evolutionary races; biologic improvement is the work of the Adamic progeny [51:5.3]. The Prince's staff conduct superior men and women to the Garden, where they voluntarily mate with the Adamic offspring, and this is considered the highest honor [51:5.3]. Racial wars and tribal struggles then diminish [51:5.4], and the children born of these unions, which follow the monogamous pledge of the violet race, are educated in the Prince's schools and then go out to the race of their parent [51:5.5]. As a result, "⟦Q 51:5.6⟧in one hundred thousand years more progress is made than in a million years of former struggle⟦/Q⟧" [51:5.6].

3. The Edenic Regime: The Second Center of World Culture

On a normal world the Garden headquarters becomes, together with the Prince's headquarters city, the second center of world culture and sets the pace of civilization [51:6.2]. While the Prince's schools deal with philosophy, religion, morals, and high intellectual and artistic achievement, the Garden schools are devoted to the practical arts, social culture, economic development, trade, and civil government [51:6.4]. The chief aim of the Adamic regime is to move mankind from the hunter and herder stages to the stage of the agriculturist and horticulturist [52:3.3]. And because the Material Son and Daughter can see the invisible Planetary Prince and explain him, they become the last link connecting God and man [51:6.5].

4. The Seven Fathers

With the passing of the ages the Material Son and Daughter become accepted as the common parents of the blended human race, and mortals who start out from an inhabited world are intended to have the experience of recognizing seven fathers [51:6.6]. These seven are: the biologic father, the father in the flesh; the father of the realm, the Planetary Adam; the father of the spheres, the System Sovereign; the Most High Father, the Constellation Father; the universe Father, the Creator Son; the super-Fathers, the Ancients of Days; and the spirit or Havona Father, the Universal Father [51:6.7-13]. The last Father is the one who, though he dwells on Paradise, bestows his spirit to live in the minds of the lowly creatures [51:6.13].

Summary

On a normal world the Planetary Adam and Eve establish the violet race and have their offspring unite voluntarily with the superior individuals of the evolutionary races, raising mankind's biologic, intellectual, and spiritual level [51:3.3, 51:5.3, 51:6.1]. As a result mankind comes to recognize seven fathers, from the father in the flesh to the Universal Father of Paradise [51:6.6], and this shows that we receive care layered upon care within the universe family.

q218.question: On a normal world peace comes after the bestowal Son appears; why has this not happened on Urantia, and how is brotherhood achieved?
q218.answer:
On a normal evolutionary world the bestowal Son comes when that world is spiritually ripe, and as the Prince of Peace he arrives with the message, "⟦Q 52:6.1⟧Peace on earth and good will among men⟦/Q⟧" [52:6.1]. On such a world the postbestowal age is a dispensation of world-wide peace [52:6.1]. But because Urantia has not proceeded in the normal order, achieving brotherhood here requires more time and effort, and religious revelation [52:6.1, 52:6.2].

1. The Postbestowal Age on a Normal World

On a normal world the bestowal Son does not appear in the flesh until the races have reached the highest levels of intellectual development and ethical attainment [52:5.1]. He meets a spiritually trained race on a world of high educational culture [52:5.3], and after his resurrection the Spirit of Truth is poured out, and every will creature of normal mind receives a Thought Adjuster upon reaching the age of moral choice [52:5.6]. In this age the practice of the golden rule becomes possible, the problems of disease and delinquency are virtually solved, and the average length of life rises well beyond three hundred years [52:5.8, 52:5.9]. Governmental supervision decreases and true self-government functions, the military arm disappears, and there is only one race, one language, and one religion [52:5.10].

2. Why Urantia Is Different

On Urantia the bestowal Son, our Creator Son, appeared, contrary to the usual order, near the close of the Adamic dispensation [52:5.1]. This world was unprepared because of a rebellious Planetary Prince and a defaulting Material Son [50:6.5]. Jesus himself warned his disciples that his advent would not bring the usual reign of peace and that there would be "⟦Q 52:6.1⟧wars and rumors of wars⟦/Q⟧" [52:6.1]. Even so, his bestowal brought a factual change on Urantia: since Pentecost mortals can again proceed directly to the morontia spheres after death [52:5.5].

3. Five Conditions of Social Brotherhood

Jesus showed the way to the immediate attainment of spiritual brotherhood, but social brotherhood depends largely on the following personal transformations and planetary adjustments [52:6.2].

Social brotherhood: International contacts through travel, commerce, and competitive play, and the development of a common language [52:6.3].

Intellectual cross-fertilization: Each race and nation coming to understand the thoughts and feelings of the others, for "⟦Q 52:6.4⟧La ignorancia produce la sospecha, y la sospecha es incompatible con la actitud esencial de compasión y amor.⟦/Q⟧" [52:6.4].

Ethical awakening: Only moral conscience can condemn the evil of national envy and racial jealousy [52:6.5].

Political wisdom: Emotional maturity replaces the arbitrament of war with international judicial techniques, while selfish political cleverness is self-destructive [52:6.6].

Spiritual insight: The brotherhood of man is ultimately predicated on the recognition of the fatherhood of God [52:6.7].

4. The Quickest Way

The Urantia Book says, "⟦Q 52:6.7⟧La manera más rápida de realizar la hermandad del hombre en Urantia consiste en efectuar la transformación espiritual de la humanidad de hoy en día.⟦/Q⟧" [52:6.7]. Applying spiritual pressure from above to augment moral insight, and enhancing the soul capacity of every person to understand and love every other person, is the only technique for accelerating social evolution [52:6.7].

Summary

On a normal world the postbestowal age is an age of peace, self-government, and high ethics [52:5.8, 52:5.10], but Urantia, because of rebellion and Adam's default, could not follow that order [52:6.1]. Brotherhood on our world is therefore achieved through social contact, mutual understanding, ethical awakening, political wisdom, and above all the personal spiritual transformation of knowing God as Father [52:6.2-7].

q219.question: As a lesson left by the Lucifer rebellion, how are true liberty and false liberty to be distinguished?
q219.answer:
The Urantia Book says that of all the confusing problems growing out of the Lucifer rebellion, none has caused more difficulty than the failure of immature mortals to distinguish between true and false liberty [54:1.1]. Lucifer's manifesto put "liberty" in the forefront, but in reality it was an attempt to rob other beings of their liberty [54:2.3]. This rebellion thus became a cosmic textbook for learning the true meaning of liberty.

True liberty is the reward of evolutionary progress, while false liberty is the subtle deception produced by the error of time and the evil of space [54:1.2].

1. The Conditions of True Liberty

The Urantia Book says, "⟦Q 54:1.2⟧La libertad duradera se basa en la realidad de la justicia —inteligencia, madurez, fraternidad y equidad.⟦/Q⟧" [54:1.2]. True liberty is progressively related to reality and always has regard for social equity, cosmic fairness, universe fraternity, and divine obligations [54:1.3]. Conversely, when liberty is divorced from material justice, intellectual fairness, social forbearance, moral duty, and spiritual values, it becomes suicidal [54:1.4]. Liberty does not exist apart from cosmic reality [54:1.4].

2. Self-Control and Self-Assertion

True liberty is the associate of genuine self-respect, and false liberty is the consort of self-admiration [54:1.6]. Again, "⟦Q 54:1.6⟧La verdadera libertad es el fruto del autocontrol; la falsa libertad, la suposición de la autoafirmación.⟦/Q⟧" [54:1.6]. Self-control leads to altruistic service, while self-admiration tends toward the exploitation of others for self-aggrandizement [54:1.6]. Unbridled self-will and unregulated self-expression are unmitigated selfishness, the acme of ungodliness, and license masquerading as liberty is the forerunner of abject bondage [54:1.5].

3. Respecting the Liberty of Others

There is no error greater than the self-deception that leads beings to crave power in order to deprive others of their natural liberties, and the golden rule of human fairness cries out against all such fraud and unfairness [54:1.8]. Even the supreme rulers of the universe mercifully stand back in respect for the prerogatives of the will, and no creature may, in the name of personal liberty, infringe the rights of his fellows [54:1.9]. The Urantia Book sums it up: "⟦Q 54:1.8⟧Tan sólo la libertad verdadera y genuina es compatible con el reino del amor y con el ministerio de la misericordia.⟦/Q⟧" [54:1.8].

4. What Did Lucifer Seek to Steal?

God has ordained that all his sons and daughters should be partners of the time-space Creators in the adventure of achieving experiential perfection, and therefore he gives them creative free will and indwells them with his spirit [54:2.2]. Lucifer's folly was the attempt to short-circuit time, and his crime was the attempt to deprive creatures of their freewill participation in the long evolutionary struggle to attain light and life [54:2.3]. His manifesto, clothed in the garments of liberty, was in reality a theft of personal liberty [54:2.3]. No being has the rightful liberty to deprive another being of "⟦Q 54:2.5⟧the right to love and be loved, the privilege of worshiping God and of serving his fellows⟦/Q⟧" [54:2.5].

Summary

True liberty is predicated on justice, maturity, and fraternity; it is the fruit of self-control and shows itself in altruistic service [54:1.2, 54:1.6]. False liberty is self-assertion and license, and it ends in bondage and self-destruction [54:1.4, 54:1.5]. The Lucifer rebellion showed that a voice crying "liberty" can in fact rob others of their liberty [54:2.3], and we become truly free when we govern ourselves and respect the rights of others.

q220.question: Why did God not destroy Lucifer and the rebels at once, but leave them for so long?
q220.answer:
The Urantia Book takes up this question directly and explains that the delay in judging the rebels was not due to impotence or indifference but was the result of justice, mercy, and wisdom working together. The purposes were to give the wrongdoer himself ample time to choose, to let all concerned beings mature their attitudes, and finally to reap a greater good even out of evil [54:3.2, 54:5.10, 54:6.6]. And at the root of it all is God as Father [54:6.2].

1. The Time Lag of Justice

Wholehearted identification with sin is in the end equivalent to annihilation, but there must always be ample time between that moment and the execution of the penalty [54:3.2]. For the judgment must be so fair as to satisfy all concerned personalities and even to win the approval of the sinner himself [54:3.2]. The Ancients of Days refuse to annihilate any being until all moral values and spiritual realities are extinct in the evildoer and in his sympathizers [54:3.3].

2. The Time Lag of Mercy

Parents who have reared children can understand why Michael, a Creator-father, is slow to condemn his sons, and Jesus' story of the prodigal son illustrates this [54:4.2]. If prolonged mercy can lead to repentance and rehabilitation, then however long the execution of justice is delayed, it is justified [54:4.3]. The ministry of mercy provides a saving interval between seedtime and harvest, and The Urantia Book says, "⟦Q 54:4.6⟧This restraint of justice by mercy proves that God is love⟦/Q⟧" [54:4.6]. Yet this delay is not endless: at the time of this revelation the first hearing was held on Uversa, and Satan too was confined to the prison world. "⟦Q 54:4.8⟧La justicia en un universo dominado por la misericordia puede ser lenta, pero es certera.⟦/Q⟧" [54:4.8].

3. The Wisdom of Delay: Several Reasons

Mercy must give every wrongdoer sufficient time to formulate a deliberate attitude [54:5.2], and justice never destroys that which mercy can save [54:5.3]. Because Michael had not yet completed his bestowal career and had not acquired unlimited sovereignty, he did not exercise summary jurisdiction [54:5.6]. The rebellion had to run its full course so that every being in Norlatiadek could fully decide its attitude; otherwise the Paradise quarantine might have been extended to the entire constellation [54:5.10]. There was also counsel that any attempt at arbitrary suppression would have led astray at least three times as many beings [54:5.12]. Time, moreover, is relative: from the standpoint of Uversa, Lucifer's crime is being brought to trial a mere two and a half seconds after it was committed [54:5.13]. It is said that forty-eight such reasons are taught on Uversa [54:5.14].

4. The Triumph of Love: Good Reaped from Evil

At first it seemed an unmitigated calamity, but the Melchizedeks now teach that the good resulting from the Satania rebellion is more than a thousand times the sum of all the evil [54:6.6]. Those who withstood the test were raised in status and spiritual value [54:6.5]. Even if we suffer temporary hardship through the wrongdoing of another, no such consequence can in the least deprive us of our divine right to the Paradise ascent and the attainment of God [54:6.4].

Summary

The delay in judging the rebels was divine wisdom: to give sinners the opportunity to repent, to let all beings decide their attitudes freely, and to reap a greater good even from evil [54:4.3, 54:5.10, 54:6.6]. Therefore we who are bound by time should be cautious in criticizing the delays of the universe administrators [54:6.8], and we can trust that the God of love governs every destiny with justice and mercy [54:6.1].

q221.question: How does light and life widen step by step from the planet to the system, the constellation, the local universe, and the superuniverse, and can an individual on an isolated world attain that status?
q221.answer:
Light and life does not end with the perfecting of a single planet. The Urantia Book describes seven stages of settledness, beginning with the planetary stage and continuing through the system, the constellation, the local universe, the minor and major sectors, and the superuniverse stage [55:7.1, 55:12.1]. And, remarkably, it says that even on an isolated world where this vast process has not yet taken place, the individual can personally attain the status of light and life [55:11.7].

1. First, the Planetary Stage

This stage begins when the Trinity Teacher Sons complete their mission and the Planetary Prince is elevated, by mandate of the bestowal Son, to the position of Planetary Sovereign [55:7.1]. The visible rulers of such a world are the Material Son and Daughter, the Planetary Adam and Eve, and the idea of kings and queens spread throughout the universe realms grew out of knowledge of this arrangement [55:7.2]. When that age comes on Urantia, there is no doubt that Machiventa Melchizedek will occupy the position of Planetary Sovereign [55:7.3]. When the most recently settled world has remained in that state for one thousand years of system time, the whole system enters the next stage [55:7.4].

2. Second and Third, the System and Constellation Stages

When an entire system is settled, the Planetary Sovereigns become members of the system conclave, the system gains virtual autonomy, and the System Sovereign is no longer changed [55:8.1, 55:8.3]. The midsoniters come and counsel, doing in the realm of philosophy and spiritualized thought what the Material Sons did biologically [55:8.4]. When the last system of a constellation is settled, the Most Highs are proclaimed rulers of unlimited authority [55:8.7]; a council of System Sovereigns functions in place of the legislative function, and in the seventh stage of settledness the Most Highs are exalted to the true dignity signified by their name [55:9.2, 55:9.3].

3. Fourth through Seventh, from the Local Universe to the Superuniverse

When a local universe is settled, a supreme council is established, consisting of one hundred Faithfuls of Days presided over by the Union of Days, and its first act is to acknowledge the continued sovereignty of the Master Creator Son [55:10.1]. At this time the finaliter corps for the first time acknowledges an authority other than Paradise [55:10.7]. It is inferred that the minor sector stage will be concerned mainly with physical equilibrium and the major sector stage with new intellectual attainments of cosmic wisdom [55:11.2, 55:11.4]. When a superuniverse is settled, it is believed that the Unqualified Supervisors of the Supreme will become the higher administrative body [55:12.3], and the settling of the entire grand universe will be the most profound event since the appearance of the central universe [55:12.5].

4. Light and Life for the Individual

The Urantia Book states clearly that the administrative order of a universe or superuniverse can never limit or delay the spiritual progress of an individual planet or mortal [55:11.6]. Younger planets may delay system unification, but they do not hinder the development of advanced worlds [55:11.7]. It says, "⟦Q 55:11.7⟧Tampoco pueden las limitaciones de medio ambiente, aun en un mundo aislado, dificultar el logro personal de un mortal específico;⟦/Q⟧" [55:11.7], and testifies that Jesus of Nazareth personally achieved the status of light and life on Urantia over nineteen hundred years ago [55:11.7]. On the worlds of light and life, too, mortals attain ever deeper communion with their Adjusters [55:6.4].

Summary

Light and life is a process of cosmic settledness that begins with the planet and widens through the system, the constellation, and the local universe to the superuniverse and the grand universe, with administration and the manifestation of Deity being newly adjusted at each stage [55:7.4, 55:8.1, 55:10.4]. Yet regardless of that vast timetable, as Jesus showed, an individual on isolated Urantia can personally live the life of light and life now [55:11.7].

q222.question: It is said that "God is unity"; please tell me how the universe is unified physically, intellectually, spiritually, and personally.
q222.answer:
Paper 56 opens with the declaration, "⟦Q 56:0.1⟧DIOS es unidad. La Deidad está coordinada universalmente.⟦/Q⟧" [56:0.1]. The universe of universes is one integrated mechanism controlled by one infinite mind, and the physical, intellectual, and spiritual domains are divinely correlated [56:0.1]. To mortals the universe may appear discordant, but those who see more broadly recognize the fundamental unity and single purpose underlying the creative diversity [56:0.2].

1. Physical Unity: Gravity and Paradise

The material creation is not infinite, but it is perfectly co-ordinated, and the source of force, energy, and power is one [56:1.1]. Paradise is the actual source of all material universes [56:1.1], and the coherence of material reality is best understood through the gravity response centered in nether Paradise [56:1.2]. The unity of gravity is universal and unchanging, and all gravity is centered in the personal presence of the Universal Father [56:1.3]. Pure energy and pure spirit are manifested diversely, yet they are one in the person of the Father, "⟦Q 56:1.4⟧because God is one⟦/Q⟧" [56:1.4].

2. Intellectual Unity: The Mind of the Infinite Spirit

Mind is the functional endowment of the Infinite Spirit and the indispensable channel of communication between spiritual realities and material realities [56:2.2]. The material evolutionary creature can recognize and comprehend the indwelling spirit only through the ministry of mind [56:2.2]. This infinite mind is bestowed as cosmic mind, from the primitive ministry of the adjutant spirits to the mind of the highest executives of the universe, and it is unified under the supervision of the Seven Master Spirits [56:2.3].

3. Spiritual Unity: The Spirit Gravity of the Eternal Son

Just as mind gravity is centered in the Infinite Spirit, universal spirit gravity is centered in the Paradise presence of the Eternal Son [56:3.1]. Spiritual phenomena, wherever met, all originate in God who is spirit, and from the local universe headquarters the Holy Spirit and the Spirit of Truth go forth to reach the material mind together with the adjutant mind-spirits [56:3.3]. When the mortal mind fuses with the Thought Adjuster, it participates in the threefold spirit endowment of the evolutionary worlds, and these three spirit manifestations are perfectly unified in the finaliter [56:3.5].

4. Personality Unity: The One Father

The Universal Father is a divinely unified personality, and personality inherently tends to unify all its constituent realities [56:4.1, 56:4.2]. The personality of mortal man, too, as a direct bestowal of the Father, has the potential of unifying the constituents of the creature, and through the personality circuit it maintains unbroken contact with the Father [56:4.2]. The Urantia Book says, "⟦Q 56:4.4⟧Para una personalidad Dios no puede ser plural.⟦/Q⟧" [56:4.4]. Philosophically we may conceive of many Deity levels and of the Trinity, but in the experience of worship God is one, our Paradise parent [56:4.5].

5. Deity Unity: Existence and Achievement

The three eternal Deity personalizations are, in the Paradise Trinity, actually one undivided Deity [56:5.1]. On Paradise and in the central universe Deity unity is a fact of existence, but in the evolving universes of time and space it is an achievement [56:5.4].

Summary

The universe is unified physically by Paradise gravity, intellectually by the mind of the Infinite Spirit, spiritually by the spirit gravity of the Eternal Son, and personally by the personality circuit of the Universal Father [56:1.3, 56:2.2, 56:3.1, 56:4.2]. And in time that unity is a task still to be achieved [56:5.4]. Therefore, when we live integrating body, mind, and spirit into one, we are taking part in the unification of the universe.

q223.question: What does it mean that the Supreme Being is "the supreme unifier," and what can we do for the Supreme Being?
q223.answer:
Paper 56 explains that the unity of Deity in time and space is in the process of being "achieved," and that the evolving Supreme Being stands at the center of this process [56:5.4, 56:6.2]. The Supreme Being functions in the experience of mortal man in three ways: as the unifier of God the Sevenfold, as the maximum of Deity that finite creatures can comprehend, and as the mortal's only avenue of approach to higher transcendental experience [56:8.1]. And remarkably, we have the opportunity to do something for and in this Supreme Being [56:8.3].

1. The Evolving Unity of Deity

The three eternal personalities of Deity are perfectly unified in the Paradise Trinity, and their offspring also reveal the unity of divinity [56:6.1]. God the Supreme, who existed as a person in Havona, at first functioned only on the spiritual level, but in the evolving universes the power of the Almighty Supreme has evolved and has been co-ordinated with his spirit person through the Supreme Mind [56:6.2]. In this way the personal reality of the Supreme Being and the power of the Almighty are being unified [56:6.2].

2. Our Path to Understanding God

The creatures of the evolutionary worlds can comprehend the unity of Deity only as it is evolving in the power-personality synthesis of the Supreme Being [56:6.3]. For on any level Deity cannot exceed the conceptual capacity of the beings of that level [56:6.3]. That is why The Urantia Book says that "⟦Q 56:6.3⟧Mortal man must, through the recognition of truth, the appreciation of beauty, and the worship of goodness, evolve the recognition of a God of love⟦/Q⟧" [56:6.3], and then progress through ascending deity levels to the comprehension of the Supreme. Ascenders comprehend the personality of the Supreme on the outer circuit of Havona, but even the finaliters have not yet actually found the Supreme Being [56:6.4].

3. God the Sevenfold and Expanding Revelation

The evolution of time and space begins on the planets presided over by the union of the Creator Son and the Creative Spirit of the local universe, and as the units of creation become settled in light and life, God the Sevenfold is more clearly revealed [56:7.2]. Each time a realm makes a new evolutionary attainment, the revelation of Deity expands simultaneously in all units of creation already organized [56:7.5]. God the Sevenfold provides a progressive approach to the Universal Father, and this approach is experientially unified in God the Supreme [56:7.8].

4. What We Can Do for the Supreme Being

The finaliters, serving in turn in all the superuniverses and accumulating experience, come to know the Supreme Being in actuality, and they are destined to serve and reveal this Supreme Deity in the future outer universes [56:8.2]. The Urantia Book says that all that the Father and his Sons do for us, we in turn have the opportunity to do for the Supreme Being, and that "⟦Q 56:8.3⟧La experiencia de amor, felicidad y servicio en el universo es mutua.⟦/Q⟧" [56:8.3]. The Father does not require that we return to him what we have received, but we can bestow it in turn upon our fellows and upon the evolving Supreme Being [56:8.3]. Even now, here on earth, we can begin the revelation of the Supreme to our fellows [56:8.4].

Summary

The Supreme Being is the evolving Deity who unifies God the Sevenfold, the Deity of time and space; who is the maximum of Deity comprehensible to finite beings; and who is the way to higher experience [56:8.1]. We come to know him through truth, beauty, and goodness [56:6.3], and we take part in his growth when we bestow the love we have received upon our fellows [56:8.3].

q224.question: In the "golden age" of a world settled in light and life, do hospitals or evil still remain? Please tell me how that society actually operates.
q224.answer:
The age of light and life is not the perfect paradise people often imagine. The Urantia Book says that the world in this age increasingly prospers under the fatherly rule of the Planetary Sovereign, but it states plainly that "⟦Q 55:3.1⟧this age is not perfect⟦/Q⟧" [55:3.1]. There are still hospitals, accidents, and old age, and there also remains actual and potential evil that stimulates choice [55:3.1, 55:3.10]. Yet compared with primitive times such a world is like Paradise, and if we were transported there we would call it heaven on earth [55:3.1].

1. What Still Remains

These worlds progress under the momentum of one language, one religion, and, on normal spheres, one race [55:3.1]. Yet there are well-appointed hospitals for the care of the sick; the problems of caring for accidental injuries and the infirmities of old age remain; disease has not been entirely vanquished, nor have the earth animals been perfectly subdued [55:3.1]. Even on such glorious spheres evil is abundantly present to stimulate choice between truth and error, good and evil [55:3.10]. Ascenders from worlds beyond the third stage are destined to temporary assignments on planets in the early stages of evolution, so even high attainment has its cost [55:3.11].

2. Public Life Funded by the Tithe

Human government dealing with material problems still functions in this age [55:3.2]. On one world of the first stage visited by the revealer, every able-bodied adult paid ten per cent of his income into the public treasury; of this, three per cent went to the promotion of truth, such as science, education, and philosophy; three per cent to beauty, such as play, leisure, and art; three per cent to goodness, such as social service, altruism, and religion; and one per cent to insurance against the risk of incapacity for work [55:3.2-6]. Natural resources were administered as the property of the community [55:3.7].

3. Honor and Co-operation

On that world the highest honor conferred upon a citizen was the order of "supreme service," and this was the only degree of recognition ever granted in the morontia temple [55:3.8]. Most social and administrative positions and judicial offices were held jointly by a man and a woman, or by married couples [55:3.9]. Children contribute more to one another's training when they are not too far apart in age, and they are trained within a competitive system for the mastery of truth, beauty, and goodness [55:3.10]. The administration includes Material Sons and Daughters, the descendants of Adam and Eve, humanized midwayers, mortals who hold the order of supreme service, commissions elected by the citizens, and others [55:3.13-20].

4. The Peak of Material Development and Urantia's Task

In more advanced stages poverty and social inequality all but disappear, war becomes a chapter of history, there are no more armies or police forces, and government gradually disappears [55:5.2, 55:5.4]. The Urantia Book says that the extent of civil government and statutory regulation is in inverse proportion to the morality and spirituality of the citizenship [55:5.4]. What, then, is the task of our world? The greatest handicaps to Urantia's attaining light and life are the problems of disease, degeneracy, war, multicolored races, and multilingualism [55:3.21], and no world can progress beyond the first stage until it has achieved one language, one religion, and one philosophy [55:3.22].

Summary

The golden age of light and life is a real world in which hospitals, accidents, and the testing of choice still remain, yet it is a mature society that devotes public resources to truth, beauty, and goodness and honors "supreme service" most highly [55:3.1, 55:3.3-5, 55:3.8]. This picture shows that utopia is achieved not by compulsion but through the morality and spirituality of the citizens [55:5.4], and it reminds us of what we should be working toward today [55:3.21, 55:3.22].
